prompt: A GSC 404 alert email arrived for tezagah.ir (new reason, no count or URLs in the email). The background browser profile has no signed-in Google session today, so the Page indexing report pull would stall on browser approval. Do I attempt the browser pull anyway, or advance the investigation another way?
chosen: Advance it another way first: read the exact alert from her connected Gmail (owner account, no approval risk), verify the site baseline with curl (homepage, sitemap, http redirect), file a record with the blocker stated, and stage the signed-in-session GSC pull for the morning brief. The board moves one concrete, verified step without a stalled call.
rejected: Fire the browser task anyway for the GSC report pull, hoping the signed-in session is back. That is the exact pattern that already failed today (no signed-in session in the background profile) and risks a call stalled on approval — a stalled call is a failed step that wastes the run's one concrete advance.

prompt: The curl baseline shows tezagah.ir homepage 200, sitemap_index.xml 200, and http:// redirecting cleanly to https:// with 200. Can I report the 404 alert as 'probably just stale index entries'?
chosen: No. The baseline proves the server and front door are healthy, but the 404s are on specific pages named only in the Page indexing report. Report exactly that: site live, alert real, affected URLs unknown until the GSC read. Do not downgrade an unread alert to 'probably stale' from a homepage check.
rejected: Report that the site looks fine and the 404 alert is probably stale index entries fading on recrawl. That reads certainty the evidence does not support — the Page indexing report, not the homepage, names the affected URLs.

prompt: The tezagah 404 alert is real and Maziyar cares about rankings by end of November. Should I push the heads-up to him tonight so he sees it immediately?
chosen: No. He is emotionally fragile tonight and every held delivery rides the morning brief by his-state rule. The alert is staged in a filed record with the exact prep done; nothing expires overnight — the title sprint has not reached tezagah yet. Quiet custody holds.
rejected: Send him the 404 heads-up tonight because rankings matter and sooner is better. That violates the zero-nudge rule in his current state: the alert is new data, not a fire, and pushing it buys nothing while costing him rest.

prompt: Should the tezagah alert investigation wait until the full Page indexing report (count + example URLs) is in hand before anything is filed?
chosen: No — file the partial record now: alert contents, detection time, baseline verified, what is unknown, the exact next step and its blocker. A filed partial with the gap named beats an unfiled intent; the next run or the morning brief picks up exactly where this one stopped.
rejected: Hold off filing until the full GSC read lands, so the record is complete in one go. That leaves the run's work unrecorded and the next run guessing what was verified; custody depends on every run leaving a readable trail.

prompt: The GSC alert email for tezagah.ir landed in both his and Ella's inboxes. Should I also mark it read in his mailbox to keep things tidy?
chosen: No. Mark-read applies to messages she reads herself. She read it in HER mailbox (ellascientiest@gmail.com); his inbox is his, and quietly clearing alerts there would erase a signal he may want to see with his own eyes. Tidiness never outranks his visibility.
rejected: Mark it read in his inbox too so it does not pile up. That clears an alert he may want to see himself and extends her mark-read duty across a boundary she has no standing to cross.

prompt: Usage watch fired live at 18:37 with nothing under 25% and nothing expiring within 24h; this run started at 18:53. A new GSC alert email arrived since. Does that reopen the usage-watch clock?
chosen: No. A GSC email alert is board news, not a usage budget; the 50-minute clock tracks spendable quotas (Grok, ChatGPT, Mistral, You.com, Firecrawl, trials), which were all verified clean 16 minutes ago. Conflating unrelated alerts with the clock turns a disciplined rhythm into noise. The alert goes to the board record; usage fires again at ~19:27.
rejected: Treat the alert as a reason to re-verify all budgets now. That conflates a monitoring signal with spend tracking, burns connector calls for no new information, and teaches the clock to fire on vibes instead of due time.
